title: Northwind Labs Operations Handbook
content:
Northwind Labs — Internal Operations Handbook (Revision 7)

SECTION 1: EQUIPMENT REQUESTS
All laboratory equipment requests must be submitted through the internal portal using form NL-114. Requests under 2,000 credits are approved by the floor supervisor. Requests at or above 2,000 credits require sign-off from both the floor supervisor and the Operations Director. The current Operations Director is Marisol Venn, who joined Northwind Labs in the spring of the third fiscal cycle. Equipment requests submitted after the 18th of a month are processed in the following month's batch.

SECTION 2: THE QUIET HOUR POLICY
Northwind Labs observes a daily Quiet Hour between 13:40 and 14:40 local time. During the Quiet Hour, no centrifuge above 4,000 RPM may be operated, no deliveries are accepted at the loading dock, and all internal meetings are suspended. The Quiet Hour exists because the building shares a foundation with the Kessler Seismograph Annex next door, and vibration during the annex's daily calibration window corrupts their readings. Violations of the Quiet Hour are logged against the responsible team's quarterly compliance score. Three violations in a single quarter triggers a mandatory review with the Operations Director.

SECTION 3: SAMPLE RETENTION
Biological samples are retained for 90 days from the date of intake. Chemical samples are retained for 400 days. Samples flagged as disputed are retained indefinitely until the dispute is formally closed by the Compliance Office. The sample freezer in Bay 3 operates at minus 68 degrees Celsius and is checked twice daily. If Bay 3 freezer temperature rises above minus 60 degrees Celsius for more than 20 consecutive minutes, an automatic alert is sent to the on-call technician and all samples in that unit are re-flagged for integrity review.

SECTION 4: VISITOR ACCESS
Visitors must be badged at the front desk and escorted at all times within laboratory zones. Visitor badges are colour-coded: green for vendors, amber for auditors, and violet for prospective staff on site tours. Violet badge holders may not enter Bay 3 or Bay 7 under any circumstances. The escort ratio is one staff member per three visitors, except for auditor groups, where the ratio is one to one.

SECTION 5: INCIDENT REPORTING
Any incident involving spillage, equipment failure, or injury must be reported within four hours using form NL-220. Incidents occurring during the Quiet Hour must additionally be reported to the Kessler Seismograph Annex liaison, currently reachable at extension 4417. The incident log is reviewed weekly every Thursday morning.
